solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fine loo rug is splashed

indicators.note: something splashed about is thrown around, so the letters of the three words before it are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A remark that the toilet mat has been sprayed is fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Glorious weather is fine weather; the two are synonyms for splendid conditions.

clue.text: Hunk appears in front of sweetheart, undressed

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting one piece in front of another sets it first in the answer

parts.note: a hunk of chocolate or soap can be a bar
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E, a crossword convention

explanation.surface: A muscular man shows up before his lover with no clothes on.
explanation.definitionFit: Bare skin is uncovered, the plain sense of having no clothes on.

clue.text: One man following another quarry

indicators.note: one name follows the other, so it comes second in the answer

parts.note: another man, here the short name Vic
one man, here the short name Tim

explanation.surface: One man trails behind another, apparently hunting him.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarry is the hunted creature, and a victim is likewise the one preyed upon.

clue.text: Duck the French order after cold salad

indicators.note: the other pieces come after the cold letter in the answer

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, shaped like the letter O
les is the French plural word for the
law and order go together; law is rule or order

explanation.surface: A diner skips the French dish and orders a chilled salad.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleslaw is a kind of salad made from shredded raw cabbage.

clue.text: Eminent man of letters?

parts.note: a man of letters is normally a writer; here it is someone in charge of the mail, and eminent means senior

explanation.definitionFit: The head of a post office is the person most senior over handling letters.

clue.text: Fast recipe in bar

indicators.note: the recipe letter is placed inside the word for bar

parts.note: a stave is a wooden bar or rod
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin, on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A quick recipe served in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like an adjective meaning quick, but it is a verb: to go without food.
explanation.definitionFit: To fast is to go without food, which is what starving means.

clue.text: Caught bending, doing housework perhaps

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
leaning is tilting or bending over

explanation.surface: Someone is spotted stooping over while doing the chores.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusting and scrubbing are household chores, the obvious example of domestic work.

clue.text: Transparent guy heartlessly embracing girl

indicators.note: embracing means holding around, so one piece wraps the other
heartlessly removes the middle letter of the word

parts.note: taken as written
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A see-through man coldly hugging a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Glass-like material can be seen through, so the two words both mean see-through.

clue.text: Origin of wine in glasses?

indicators.note: the wine sits inside the glasses, as the surface says

parts.note: a pair of spectacles looks like two letter Os side by side
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Where the wine being drunk from these glasses first came from.
explanation.walkthrough: Port is named after the Portuguese city, so the whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Portuguese city is where port wine was shipped from and gets its name.

clue.text: Generous entry charge to catch Queen

indicators.note: to catch means to hold inside, so the queen letter is caught within the charge

parts.note: a fee is a charge paid for entry
R, for Regina, is the abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: Admission is generously waived so that people can see the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A free-handed giver is liberal or lavish with money.

clue.text: Jet to carry bombs in flight

indicators.note: bombs suggests something blown apart, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A warplane designed to carry bombs while airborne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bombs' looks like the cargo but is the anagram signal; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight path is the curved route an object follows through the air.

clue.text: Stand in quiet disapproval

parts.note: P stands for piano, quiet in music
odium is hatred or strong disapproval

explanation.surface: Standing in silent protest.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised platform for a speaker or conductor is a stand they mount.

clue.text: One on a bender it turned out, drunk

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece on another is set above it, so first

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: turned out suggests something reshaped, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone out on a drinking spree ended up intoxicated.
explanation.walkthrough: A bender is British slang for a drinking spree, which fits the definition nicely.
explanation.definitionFit: Inebriated is a formal synonym for intoxicated.

clue.text: Rescues from attacks around middle of hostilities

indicators.note: the word for attacks goes round the middle letter

parts.note: savages is a verb here: mauls or attacks fiercely

indicators.note: the middle of the word is its central letter, the sixth of eleven

explanation.surface: Someone saves people from assaults amid fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: To salvage something is to save it from loss or wreckage.

clue.text: Country united in part of Japanese capital

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: the sen is a small coin, a hundredth part of the Japanese yen
wed means joined or united in marriage

explanation.surface: A country joined together in a district of Tokyo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' reads as Tokyo, but it is money: the yen, of which the sen is a part.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the Scandinavian nation, an example of a country.

clue.text: Former wife with stories about one's feats

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: the stories go about, that is around, the one

parts.note: plots are the storylines of stories
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: An ex-wife tells tales about someone's achievements.
explanation.definitionFit: Exploits are bold deeds or adventures, the same as feats.

clue.text: Bandage what's damaged joining bone tip

indicators.note: damaged letters are knocked out of shape, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the contraction stands for what is, so its S counts as a letter

indicators.note: the tip here is the end letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone asks what has been hurt, while strapping a broken bone.
explanation.definitionFit: To swathe is to wrap something in cloth, as with a bandage.

clue.text: Army unit upset over man coming out

indicators.note: in a down entry, over puts one piece above the other
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so read the unit backwards

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps
a gent is a gentleman, a man

explanation.surface: A distressed soldier's unit is bothered by a man leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Something emergent is appearing or rising into view.

clue.text: Tense pose with painter, rising painter

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading upwards, so the whole run is backwards

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
to sit is to pose for a portrait
RA is a Royal Academician, a painter

explanation.surface: An artist's model sits stiffly with a painter, then stands up.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist is anyone who paints pictures, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Cheeky devil facing lash by headmaster finally

indicators.note: facing means set in front of the next piece

parts.note: an imp is a little devil
to lash is to tie with rope

indicators.note: finally picks the end letter of the word

explanation.surface: A naughty little devil about to be whipped by the head teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Impudent behaviour is unseemly, so both words mean rude or out of line.

clue.text: Butch, no good inside, getting butcher

indicators.note: the no good letters go inside the other word

parts.note: butch means manly, masculine, so male

explanation.surface: A tough guy, useless deep down, takes a job as a meat seller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butcher' looks like a noun, the trade; here it is the verb, to hack or ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: To mangle something is to mutilate or ruin it, as a butcher would.

clue.text: Scoundrel's almost lascivious following bird

indicators.note: the second piece follows the first in the answer

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible scoundrel

indicators.note: almost cuts off the last letter of the word

parts.note: lewd means lascivious

explanation.surface: A rogue's leering admirer is close behind.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a long-billed wading bird, an example of a bird.

clue.text: Small parts showed up on stage initially

parts.note: came means arrived or showed up

indicators.note: initially takes the first letters of the words

explanation.surface: Bit parts appeared at the start of a play.
explanation.definitionFit: Cameos are brief appearances by actors, little roles in a film or play.

clue.text: Man in toga's set about opposition

indicators.note: set about suggests rearranging, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: here the S counts as a letter, as in toga is

explanation.surface: A Roman figure in his robe is attacked out of hostility.
explanation.definitionFit: Antagonism is hostility or active opposition between people.

clue.text: Starts to tow unusually gigantic ship

definitions.text: Starts to tow unusually gigantic ship

indicators.note: starts to means take the opening letter of each word that follows

explanation.surface: Small powered boats begin pulling a huge vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes what these boats do, which is why it reads as both definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Tugboats are small vessels used to tow big ships into harbour.

clue.text: Old ship seen on English Channel?

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: a tub is a slang word for an old, slow ship

explanation.surface: A vintage vessel spotted on the English Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English Channel' is the obvious phrase, but 'English' gives E and 'Channel' is the definition, a pipe or duct.
explanation.definitionFit: A tube is a pipe or duct, a channel for liquid or gas.

clue.text: Inscribed in Gospel: destroying the first-born

indicators.note: inscribed in means written inside the words that follow, so the letters lie within them

explanation.surface: A Bible text about the killing of first-born children.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the plague on the first-born in Exodus.
explanation.definitionFit: The eldest child is the one born first in a family.

clue.text: Instrument bent with room to manoeuvre

indicators.note: manoeuvre means move around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bent brass instrument needs plenty of space for its slide.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a brass wind instrument with a slide, an example of an instrument.
